<!-- pr-reviewer: bf2dcaa785d88726d9fc32f2406ee3794ebbe783 -->
**Clean delta: ready for the maintainer, as a stacked PR (safety tier, P1 #1641).**

Range reviewed: `da340c0f..bf2dcaa7` only (one commit, no merge commits in the range, so no remerge-diff). Merge order: #1615 -> #1622 -> #1634 -> #1640 -> #1644. This PR is stacked on #1615, which carries NeoTech's needs-rework, so I set no label and removed none; that review stays open until its own head is cleared.

**What looks good**
- `keep_law::kept_models` (keep_law.rs:183-187) admits a cross drill. It is the same `neighbour_parts` set #1621 uses: the setup's other parts, with the source, fixtures and a stock-only model left out.
- `cross_part::neighbours_clear` (cross_part.rs:117-155) sweeps the whole finished chain with `verify::solid_hits_walled` and no hole wall excused (`&[]`). The chain is every move of the one toolpath, so feeds, retracts, rapids and the links between holes are all swept, and shank and holder are included (`ShankHit`, `RapidInStock`, `Gouge` are all named). It is called on both the on-origin and the shifted-spindle return in `cross_spindle::cross_drill` (cross_spindle.rs:136-137, 160), always after `part_clear`.
- With no neighbours it returns `Ok` at once, so a single-part setup and a stock-source cross drill (which passes `&[]`) take the same path as on #1640. I confirmed this by reading the code; I did not diff posted NC against main. The "clear of A" pin posts on both stocks.
- No unwrap/expect/panic or unchecked indexing in the new code (`.get`, `let ... else`). Files: cross_part 208, cross_spindle 343, keep_law 197, new test 299; generate.rs is 3599 lines (already far over, growth is +15). Provenance and decision record present (`docs/decisions/1641-cross-drill-neighbours.md`); body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1641`.

**Results (locally, on the PR head including its stack; no runner: stacked on unmerged PRs, and the base is not main, so no trial merge was made)**
- `cross_drill_neighbours` 5/5, `stock_source_cross_drill` 6/6, `keep_law` 7/7, `neighbour_law` 5/5, `drilling_cross_part` 3/3, `drilling_cross_spindle` 7/7, `lathe_cross_drill` 5/5: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mutations I ran myself (each alone, then reverted):
  - M2, `neighbours_clear` not called: 4 red (into, approach, tube, MCP); the "clear" pin stays green.
  - M3, source hole walls excused on the neighbours: red on `a_neighbours_round_hole_on_the_line_is_not_excused` only.
  - M1, cross drill out of `kept_models`: 4 red, as claimed.
  - Probe M4 (below).

**On the unguarded M4 ("redundant second check")**
It is not redundant, and it is not provably inert. I removed `neighbours_clear` and added a temporary probe at the tail (generate.rs:3192). The tail neighbour law still fires on the chain: 0 warnings before, 10 after (`Gouge` / `RapidInStock` alternating), and they are `blocks_post()` findings. The pins then fail only because they demand a refusal naming the hole. So the tail is a real second net: it keeps the post blocked, unnamed, if `neighbours_clear` ever misses. It also judges with a different tolerance (`excess_floor`, `stl`, `CONTAIN_STEP`) and a different step, so I cannot show it never changes a verdict. Deleting it is therefore not free. Dead on its face is not the case either way, but it is unguarded and its comment (generate.rs:2900-2902) is true. My recommendation is to keep it and, ideally, pin it with a test that asserts a blocking finding on a chain the radial law passes; that is not blocking. If the maintainer prefers fewer unguarded lines, removing it is defensible only after that pin shows what it catches.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The conservative cost the decision record names stands: a drill meant to pass through a neighbour's existing bore is refused. Reasonable for the safety tier.
- Not exercised by the author and not by me: a plain lathe holding two parts, the 3+2 frame arm, MCP on a turned stock.
- Windows-only readings: none touched.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: bf2dcaa785d88726d9fc32f2406ee3794ebbe783 -->
**Clean delta: no blockers. Stacked, so it waits for its parents #1615 (open requested change), #1622, #1634 and #1640; no merge-ready label is set until they merge.** Range reviewed: `da340c0f..bf2dcaa7` only; the parents are reviewed on their own PRs. Safety tier (P1 #1641).

## What looks good
- `keep_law::kept_models` now admits a part-source cross drill (`is_cross_drill`), so `neighbour_parts` is no longer empty for it (keep_law.rs, the `kept_models` arm).
- `cross_part::neighbours_clear` sweeps the finished posed chain (drill, shank, holder, rapids) against the other parts with no hole wall excused (empty walls argument), and refuses by name with the hole's line. It runs on and off the work offset (cross_spindle.rs, both return paths). A stock-source cross drill passes `neighbours: &[]` (#1635 already judges its stock's parts).
- Both directions are pinned in `crates/app/tests/cross_drill_neighbours.rs`: refused (into A, approach only, a neighbour's round bore on the line not excused, MCP parity) and clear posts (far side and 2 mm over the drill; aligned and turned; bar and box stock). Per the author's mutation table, removing the cross drill from `kept_models` (the old behaviour) turns the into, approach, tube and MCP pins red, so they fail on the old code. The clear-posts pin guards against over-refusal. I did not re-run the mutations.
- solid.rs 190-195 (the rapid-lift skip from #1615): this delta does not touch `crates/sim`, and that skip requires an upright pose (`axis.is_none()`); a cross-drill chain is posed along a horizontal axis, so it does not apply. The delta does not depend on #1615's open finding.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/1641-cross-drill-neighbours.md` is present with readings, mutations, dropped options and not-exercised. Body has Changelog, `Fixes #1641`, not-exercised and effort. Test file carries provenance and a gate map.
- File sizes: generate.rs 3599 (was 3590, +9; already far over 400, flagged, not blocking); cross_part.rs 208, cross_spindle.rs 343, keep_law.rs 197, new test file 299.

## Results merged with main (22b8fe7a)
On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43573282137 - success.
- Quick gate: sim suites ok, motion suites ok, app suites ok, ui suites ok (0 failed, 21.9 min).
- Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run locally: the delta has no `cfg(windows)` or per-OS pinned lines.

## Requested before merge
None on this delta.

## Notes (not blocking)
- The author's M4 (the 2D tail's neighbour law left on as a second net) is unpinned by design; fine.
- A neighbour's existing bore on the hole line is refused conservatively; documented.
- A stock-source cross drill still excuses declared holes' walls on other parts (#1635), as the decision file states.
- Not exercised: a plain lathe with two parts, the 3+2 frame arm, MCP on a turned stock.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
